problemStatement.formal: three_ordering_product_conjecture (a b c : ℕ) (ha : c < b) (hb : b < a) : ballotRatio a b * ballotRatio b c * ballotRatio a c = (a - b) * (b - c) * (a - c) / ((a + b) * (b + c) * (a + c))
problemStatement.plain: Given m candidates with vote totals a₁ > a₂ > ... > aₘ, the probability that the ordering is maintained throughout the count equals the product ∏_{i<j} (aᵢ - aⱼ)/(aᵢ + aⱼ) of pairwise ballot probabilities. This MacMahon-LGV formula connects the m-candidate ballot problem to non-intersecting lattice paths via the Lindström-Gessel-Viennot lemma.
whyMatters: Unifies m classical ballot theorems into a single determinantal formula
Demonstrates the LGV lemma in a concrete, beautiful combinatorial setting
Provides 6 verified numerical examples of the 3-candidate formula
Establishes the 2-candidate case from Mathlib's ballot theorem
